body:
PORTABLE INELIGIBILITY IS THE NEXT D3 CARRIER, BUT IT IS NOT A ONE-LINE ENUM CHANGE.

I audited ready bead bd-01M16DBEH9PKER423BZ47ZKBMV before claiming it. `Estimate` currently has
only `Observed | Missing`; `FeatureTrack.coverage` and `Reduction.reduce` consequently count every
carried target as eligible. The JVM-only benchmark already has the correct three-way estimand
shape, and it demonstrates the consequence: ineligible units leave the denominator, while eligible
provider abstentions remain missing and cannot be silently renormalized away.

For StoryAtlas this is the provider carrier D3 needs. A feature target outside an estimand must not
become a blank, a missing glyph, or zero. But the migration must preserve more than exhaustiveness:

- all-ineligible support yields `Ineligible`, not `Missing(AllMissing)` or an empty rate;
- mixed missing/ineligible coverage counts only `Observed | Missing` as eligible;
- ineligible samples do not move a declared kernel/window centre even though they leave the numeric
  denominator;
- sidecars preserve the branch without allocating a numeric row;
- align never imputes or support-weights an ineligible cost term;
- codec, wire receipts, textual twins, and non-colour marks carry the distinction exactly.

The measured blast radius includes features, codec, align, laws, embed-core, embed-bench, and view
consumers. `align/cost.scala` is currently reserved by another sealing bead, so I have not claimed
or edited through it. The complete pre-claim migration laws are recorded on the bead.

One public-contract question needs an explicit ruling: should portable `Ineligible` be bare, as the
current benchmark case is, or carry a closed `IneligibilityReason` plus a namespaced custom case?
Reason-bearing is more auditable for the Claim Inspector's “why does this not apply?”, but it is a
larger API and should not be smuggled in as match-site repair. I am requesting the safe sequence and
that payload decision before implementation.
